openItems.explanation: Setup, delivery and sales tax went to expense. The compact track loader cost $68,500.00. Getting it delivered and ready to use cost another $9,617.00: setup $1,250.00, delivery $1,950.00 and sales tax $6,417.00. Those charges went to expense, so Equipment is understated by $9,617.00 and October’s expenses are overstated by the same amount. Depreciation would also be too low for the compact track loader’s whole life.

Entered twice: AP-10409 and AP-10419. Bluepine Concrete Works invoice BPW-5188 was entered as “BPW-5188” on October 10, 2026 and again as “BPW 5188” on October 21, 2026. Same vendor, same $14,615.00. Paying both would pay Bluepine Concrete Works twice.

Billed to Property Holdings, booked in Services LLC. Windrow Landscape Care billed HANGS Property Holdings LLC, but the bill was entered in HANGS Construction Services LLC. That overstates the Services LLC’s expenses by $3,860.00. If the Services LLC pays the vendor, Property Holdings owes it $3,860.00 through the Due To and Due From accounts. Property Holdings’ own history agrees: 9 of 9 bills from Windrow Landscape Care were booked there.

Delivery, installation and sales tax went to expense. The site office unit cost $42,800.00. Getting it delivered and ready to use cost another $10,796.40: delivery $2,600.00, installation $3,900.00 and sales tax $4,296.40. Those charges went to expense, so Site Office Units is understated by $10,796.40 and October’s expenses are overstated by the same amount. Depreciation would also be too low for the site office unit’s whole life.
Over Morgan’s approval limit. Morgan Lee (Controller) approved $53,596.40, but the Controller’s limit is $50,000.00. Jordan Hale (CFO) needs to approve it.

Charged to Job 26-04, invoice says Job 27-05. The invoice is for Job 27-05 (Larkfield Commerce Park), but it was charged to Job 26-04 (Brookstone Closeout). Brookstone Closeout’s costs are overstated and Larkfield Commerce Park’s are understated by $7,980.00, which throws off both jobs’ margins.

Approved by the wrong project manager. Sam Whitaker approved it as a Job 26-04 bill. The invoice is for Job 27-05 (Larkfield Commerce Park), which is Dana Ortiz’s job, so Dana Ortiz needs to approve it.

The robotic total station was expensed. The robotic total station is one item costing $6,480.00 that will be used for years, so CAP-1 makes it a fixed asset. It was booked to 6200 Small Tools & Supplies. The whole $7,076.16, including its sales tax, belongs in 1500 Equipment, and it gets depreciated over its life.
Over Dana’s approval limit. Dana Ortiz (Project Manager) approved $18,900.00, but a project manager’s limit is $10,000.00. Morgan Lee (Controller) needs to approve it.

Approval covers only the subtotal. Dana Ortiz approved $9,800.00, the subtotal before tax. The invoice total is $10,333.60, which is over a project manager’s $10,000.00 limit. Morgan Lee (Controller) needs to approve the full amount.

Booked $14,030.00, invoice says $14,300.00. The bill was entered as $14,030.00, but the invoice total is $14,300.00. The $270.00 gap divides evenly by 9, which is the usual sign of two swapped digits. Payables and job cost are understated by $270.00.

Booked as repairs & maintenance, with no job. Rough-in plumbing is a construction cost of Job 27-05 (Larkfield Commerce Park), but it was booked to 6300 Repairs & Maintenance with no job. The job’s cost is understated by $8,460.00 and October’s expenses are overstated by the same amount. All 14 of Quarry Bend Plumbing’s past bills went to 1400 · 15-400 Plumbing.

New vendor with no W-9 on file. Brightwater Concrete Pumping was added as a vendor on October 24, 2026, and there is no signed W-9 on file. Hold the $3,150.00 payment until it arrives. The coding is fine: the Cost Code Guide puts concrete and pumping under 03-100 Concrete.

Booked bill with no invoice on file. AP-10423 for Kestrel Ridge Equipment invoice KRE-2219 ($2,336.88) is waiting to be paid, but the capture export has no invoice for it. Get the invoice before paying. Until it arrives there is nothing to check the amount, job or approval against.

Invoice is not in the books. Stonewick Roofing billed $7,150.00 for work the invoice says was finished on October 29, but there is no booked bill for it. Without an accrual, October’s costs and payables are understated by $7,150.00. A person decides whether the work belongs in October.
